q: A plant disease is usually defined as abnormal ____ and/or dysfunction of a plant.
e: A plant disease is usually defined as abnormal growth and/or dysfunction of a plant. That missing piece is growth.

q: Diseases are the result of some disturbance in the normal ____ process of the plant.
e: Diseases are the result of some disturbance in the normal life process of the plant. Write life in the gap.

q: Diseases may be the result of living and/or ____ causes.
e: Diseases may be the result of living and/or non-living causes. That missing piece is non-living.

q: Biotic diseases are caused by ____ organisms (e.g., fungi, bacteria, and viruses).
e: Biotic diseases are caused by living organisms (e.g., fungi, bacteria, and viruses). The blank is living.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living ____ conditions (e.g., soil compaction, wind, frost, soil salt damage, and girdling roots).
e: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living environmental conditions (e.g., soil compaction, wind, frost, soil salt damage, and girdling roots). The blank is environmental.

q: Plant disease is any abnormal condition that alters the appearance or ____ of a plant.
e: Plant disease is any abnormal condition that alters the appearance or function of a plant. Write function in the gap.

q: Most plant diseases, around ____ percent are caused by fungal or fungal-like organisms.
e: Most plant diseases, around 85 percent are caused by fungal or fungal-like organisms. That missing piece is 85.

q: Certain ____ also cause plant diseases.
e: Certain nematodes also cause plant diseases. The blank is nematodes.

q: Nematodes are very tiny ____.
e: Nematodes are very tiny roundworms. Write roundworms in the gap.

q: Some plant diseases are classified as "____," or diseases that are non-infectious and include damage from air pollution, nutritional deficiencies or toxicities.
e: Some plant diseases are classified as "abiotic," or diseases that are non-infectious and include damage from air pollution, nutritional deficiencies or toxicities. Write abiotic in the gap.

q: Infectious plant diseases are caused by a ____ organism such as a fungus, bacterium, mycoplasma, virus, viroid, nematode, or parasitic flowering plant.
e: Infectious plant diseases are caused by a pathogenic organism such as a fungus, bacterium, mycoplasma, virus, viroid, nematode, or parasitic flowering plant. Write pathogenic in the gap.

q: An infectious agent is capable of ____ within or on its host and spreading from one susceptible host to another.
e: An infectious agent is capable of reproducing within or on its host and spreading from one susceptible host to another. Write reproducing in the gap.

q: Non-infectious plant diseases are caused by ____ growing conditions, including extremes of temperature.
e: Non-infectious plant diseases are caused by unfavourable growing conditions, including extremes of temperature. Write unfavourable in the gap.

q: Because non-infectious causal agents are not organisms capable of reproducing within a host, they are not ____.
e: Because non-infectious causal agents are not organisms capable of reproducing within a host, they are not transmissible. That missing piece is transmissible.

q: The study of plant diseases is called plant ____.
e: The study of plant diseases is called plant pathology. The blank is pathology.

q: Pathology is derived from the two Greek words pathos (suffering, disease) and ____ (discourse, study).
e: Pathology is derived from the two Greek words pathos (suffering, disease) and logos (discourse, study). Write logos in the gap.

q: Plant pathology thus means a study of plant ____.
e: Plant pathology so means a study of plant diseases. Write diseases in the gap.

q: Plant disease is caused by a pathogen (biotic or infectious disease) or an ____ factor (abiotic or non-infectious disease).
e: Plant disease is caused by a pathogen (biotic or infectious disease) or an environmental factor (abiotic or non-infectious disease). The blank is environmental.

q: Biotic diseases can spread throughout one plant and also may spread to ____ plants of the same species.
e: Biotic diseases can spread throughout one plant and also may spread to neighbouring plants of the same species. That missing piece is neighbouring.

q: Biotic diseases sometimes show physical evidence (signs) of the pathogen, such as fungal growth, bacterial ____, or nematode cysts.
e: Biotic diseases sometimes show physical evidence (signs) of the pathogen, such as fungal growth, bacterial ooze, or nematode cysts. That missing piece is ooze.

q: Many plant problems, especially biotic problems, if not recognized and controlled early in their development, they can result in significant ____ damage for the producer.
e: Many plant problems, especially biotic problems, if not recognized and controlled early in their development, they can result in significant economic damage for the producer. That missing piece is economic.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by nonliving factors, such as drought stress, sunscald, freeze injury, wind injury, chemical injury, nutrient ____, or improper cultural practices.
e: Abiotic diseases are caused by nonliving factors, such as drought stress, sunscald, freeze injury, wind injury, chemical injury, nutrient deficiency, or improper cultural practices. That missing piece is deficiency.

q: Abiotic damage often occurs on many plant ____.
e: Abiotic damage often occurs on many plant species. Write species in the gap.

q: In contrast, biotic disease problems are more limited to a certain ____.
e: In contrast, biotic disease problems are more limited to a certain species. The blank is species.

q: For example, the fungi that cause tomato leaf blight do not cause damage on sweet ____.
e: The fungi that cause tomato leaf blight do not cause damage on sweet corn. That missing piece is corn.

q: Abiotic damage does not ____ from plant to plant over time.
e: Abiotic damage does not spread from plant to plant over time. Write spread in the gap.

q: Abiotic diseases do not show the presence of disease ____.
e: Abiotic diseases do not show the presence of disease signs. That missing piece is signs.

q: Plant diseases occurrence and severity result from the impact of three factors: the host plant, the pathogen and the ____ conditions.
e: Plant diseases occurrence and severity result from the impact of three factors: the host plant, the pathogen and the environmental conditions. Write environmental in the gap.

q: Signs of plant disease are physical ____ of the pathogen.
e: Signs of plant disease are physical evidence of the pathogen. The blank is evidence.

q: Signs can also help with plant disease ____.
e: Signs can also help with plant disease identification. That missing piece is identification.

q: Signs are the actual ____ causing the disease.
e: Signs are the actual organisms causing the disease. That missing piece is organisms.

q: Signs include conks, fruiting bodies, mildew, mushrooms, mycelium, rhizomorphs, slime flux or ooze, spore masses, insects and/or their ____.
e: Signs include conks, fruiting bodies, mildew, mushrooms, mycelium, rhizomorphs, slime flux or ooze, spore masses, insects and/or their frass. The blank is frass.

q: ____ are visible effects of disease on plants.
e: Symptoms are visible effects of disease on plants. Write Symptoms in the gap.

q: Any detectable changes in colour, shape, and/or functions of the plant in response to a pathogen or disease-causing agent is a ____.
e: Any detectable changes in colour, shape, and/or functions of the plant in response to a pathogen or disease-causing agent is a symptom. The blank is symptom.

q: Symptoms of disease are the plant's ____ to the causal agent.
e: Symptoms of disease are the plant's reaction to the causal agent. Write reaction in the gap.

q: Plant symptoms include blight, canker, chlorosis, decline, dieback, distortion, gall or gall-like, gummosis, leaf distortion, leaf scorch, leaf spot, mosaic, necrosis, stunting, wilt, witches' broom, insect feeding ____.
e: Plant symptoms include blight, canker, chlorosis, decline, dieback, distortion, gall or gall-like, gummosis, leaf distortion, leaf scorch, leaf spot, mosaic, necrosis, stunting, wilt, witches' broom, insect feeding injury. The blank is injury.

q: Viruses cause mottling, spots, mosaic-like patterns, crinkling, and other malformations on leaves and ____.
e: Viruses cause mottling, spots, mosaic-like patterns, crinkling, and other malformations on leaves and fruits. That missing piece is fruits.

q: Because viruses are ____, infected plants must be rogued or discarded.
e: Because viruses are systemic, infected plants must be rogued or discarded. That missing piece is systemic.

q: Common virus diseases in plants include curly top virus in tomatoes, cucumber ____ virus in tomatoes and vine crops.
e: Common virus diseases in plants include curly top virus in tomatoes, cucumber mosaic virus in tomatoes and vine crops. That missing piece is mosaic.

q: Fungi and fungal-like organisms (FLOs) cause more plant diseases than any other group of plant pest with over ____ species shown to cause disease.
e: Fungi and fungal-like organisms (FLOs) cause more plant diseases than any other group of plant pest with over 8,000 species shown to cause disease. That missing piece is 8,000.

q: FLOs are organisms like Pythium and Phytophthora and cause downy ____.
e: FLOs are organisms like Pythium and Phytophthora and cause downy mildew. Write mildew in the gap.

q: Most pathogenic fungi belong to the following genera: Alternaria, Aspergillus, Botrytis, Fusarium, Puccinia, Rhizopus, and ____.
e: Most pathogenic fungi belong to the following genera: Alternaria, Aspergillus, Botrytis, Fusarium, Puccinia, Rhizopus, and sclerotinia. That missing piece is sclerotinia.

q: Alternaria causes leaf spots and ____ of various plants.
e: Alternaria causes leaf spots and blight of various plants. The blank is blight.

q: Aspergillus causes rots of ____.
e: Aspergillus causes rots of seeds. Write seeds in the gap.

q: Puccinia causes ____ of cereals.
e: Puccinia causes rust of cereals. The blank is rust.

q: Rhizopus causes soft rot of ____.
e: Rhizopus causes soft rot of fruits. Write fruits in the gap.

q: Sclerotinia causes soft rot of ____.
e: Sclerotinia causes soft rot of vegetables. Write vegetables in the gap.

q: Not all bacteria are bad for plants and soil; in fact, most are ____.
e: Not all bacteria are bad for plants and soil; in fact, most are beneficial. That missing piece is beneficial.

q: There are approximately ____ types of bacteria that cause diseases in plants.
e: There are approximately 200 types of bacteria that cause diseases in plants. The blank is 200.

q: Bacteria that cause plant diseases are most active in warm and ____ environments.
e: Bacteria that cause plant diseases are most active in warm and humid environments. The blank is humid.

q: Most plant pathogenic bacteria belong to the following genera: Agrobacterium, Erwinia, Pseudomonas, Streptomyces and ____.
e: Most plant pathogenic bacteria belong to the following genera: Agrobacterium, Erwinia, Pseudomonas, Streptomyces and xanthomonas. The blank is xanthomonas.

q: Nematodes are simple, multicellular animals and are bilaterally symmetrical, soft-bodied, non-segmented ____.
e: Nematodes are simple, multicellular animals and are bilaterally symmetrical, soft-bodied, non-segmented roundworms. The blank is roundworms.

q: Most nematode species that attack plants are ____.
e: Most nematode species that attack plants are microscopic. The blank is microscopic.

q: Plant parasitic nematodes have a ____, a piercing mouthpart.
e: Plant parasitic nematodes have a stylet, a piercing mouthpart. The blank is stylet.

q: The presence of a stylet is the key diagnostic sign differentiating plant parasitic nematodes from all other types of ____.
e: The presence of a stylet is the key diagnostic sign differentiating plant parasitic nematodes from all other types of nematodes. That missing piece is nematodes.

q: Root-knot nematodes belong to the genus ____.
e: Root-knot nematodes belong to the genus meloidogyne. Write meloidogyne in the gap.

q: Plant diseases caused by infectious pathogens have seriously affected human society and nature through their damages to food production, ____ development.
e: Plant diseases caused by infectious pathogens have seriously affected human society and nature through their damages to food production, economic development. That missing piece is economic.

q: To prevent, mitigate or control plant diseases, different approaches can be used: biological, physical and ____.
e: To prevent, mitigate or control plant diseases, different approaches can be used: biological, physical and chemical. The blank is chemical.

q: Biological control is control of plant diseases using living ____.
e: Biological control is control of plant diseases using living microorganisms. Write microorganisms in the gap.

q: Physical methods of disease prevention are based on the physiological ____ of disease agents to adverse conditions.
e: Physical methods of disease prevention are based on the physiological tolerance of disease agents to adverse conditions. That missing piece is tolerance.

q: Physical control involves the removal of pathogen sources or presence of physical ____ to prevent contact between the disease agent and the host.
e: Physical control involves the removal of pathogen sources or presence of physical barriers to prevent contact between the disease agent and the host. That missing piece is barriers.

q: Chemicals used to control bacteria (____), fungi (fungicides), and nematodes (nematicides) may be applied to seeds, foliage, flowers, fruit, or soil.
e: Chemicals used to control bacteria (bactericides), fungi (fungicides), and nematodes (nematicides) may be applied to seeds, foliage, flowers, fruit, or soil. That missing piece is bactericides.

q: Chemicals used to control fungi are known as ____.
e: Chemicals used to control fungi are known as fungicides. The blank is fungicides.

q: Chemicals used to control nematodes are known as ____.
e: Chemicals used to control nematodes are known as nematicides. The blank is nematicides.
